title: SNK vs. Capcom: The Match of the Millennium
subtitle: A crossover that fits in a pocket
summary: SNK vs. Capcom: The Match of the Millennium is SNK's portable crossover fighter, released for Neo Geo Pocket Color in December 1999.
body: SNK vs. Capcom: The Match of the Millennium is SNK's portable crossover fighter, released for Neo Geo Pocket Color in December 1999. Characters from the two companies meet in a compact, animated style, bringing their recognizable attacks to a handheld contest. The player can choose a single fighter, a two-person tag team or a three-person team. Those formats make the same roster useful in different ways, from mastering one character to deciding how several fighters should share the course of a match.

The choice of gauge system adds another layer. Average mode follows a Capcom-style level meter, Counter uses an SNK-style charge gauge, and Rush strengthens super attacks when its meter fills. That decision changes how a fighter builds towards a powerful move. Rival encounters interrupt the tournament, while the final opponents connect the chosen character to the opposing company's world. Reaching the full ending also opens a character-unlocking sequence, giving the single-player journey another reward beyond simply winning the last ordinary fight.

Olympic mode turns the crossover into a broader collection of challenges, including survival and time-attack events alongside minigames inspired by Metal Slug and Ghosts 'n Goblins. Performance earns Versus points that can unlock special attacks. Link features also connect the cartridge to other compatible games, including Dreamcast releases. The small device becomes a meeting place for several arcade traditions, combining a carefully structured fighting game with playful references to the characters and genres surrounding it. Later reissues brought the handheld original to Switch and Windows.
